protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: The primary correctly showed that GoodsCategory.image is authenticated and ImageIO-gated, so the advisory's PR:N/plain-webshell narrative is inaccurate. It missed a surviving same-endpoint write primitive in tag 1.12.19: with erupt.keepUploadFileName=true, EruptFileService.createPath retains attacker-controlled ../ segments from MultipartFile.getOriginalFilename(), upload concatenates that path to erupt.uploadPath without normalization, and a valid image/polyglot passes ImageIO.read before transferTo writes outside the upload root. This is configuration-dependent authenticated arbitrary file write, not an unauthenticated unrestricted non-image upload.

findings: CVE.org remains PUBLISHED and GHSA withdrawn_at remains null; the four-line gist has no PoC, but absence of a PoC is not proof that the code path is safe.

GoodsCategory.image in erupt-example uses AttachmentType.Type.IMAGE and authVerify defaults true, so the primary is right that the published PR:N and plain-webshell description overstate the reachable mechanism.

The primary's conclusion that static resource serving and ImageIO eliminate all code-execution risk ignores attacker-controlled path escape when original filenames are retained; ImageIO accepts parseable image/polyglot content and does not sanitize the filename used by transferTo.
The later exact path-normalization fix contradicts the primary assertion that there was nothing to patch and supplies a direct source-to-sink closure absent from the primary record.

corrected_fields.bug_semantics: The advisory wording is inaccurate: GoodsCategory.image is authenticated and rejects content that ImageIO cannot parse. Nevertheless, erupt 1.12.19 has a configuration-dependent arbitrary-file-write path on that endpoint when keepUploadFileName=true: a crafted original filename can escape erupt.uploadPath, while a valid image/polyglot satisfies the IMAGE check. Treat this as a real authenticated path-traversal upload issue rather than an unauthenticated plain-webshell upload.
corrected_fields.flaw_origin: Commit 1405b8b1fe76842514d915f360c731db14b80324 first introduced the upload source-to-sink using the raw original filename and an unchecked destination under uploadPath. Its immediate parent lacked the upload implementation. Commit 8389cc152b593dca76898050517cb23706c14f58 later made random naming default but preserved the vulnerable behavior behind keepUploadFileName.
